finding.finding: Untouched R6 copper carries widespread debris: overlapping duplicate tracks, sub-50 µm segments and jogs, including on power, USB and pyro nets.
finding.evidence:
Overlapping or near-touching same-net parallel pairs: 76.
- USB_LIMITED: 0.3/0.4 mm doubled for 10.5 mm at x 28.7–28.725 and 6.1 mm at x 29.1–29.125.
- CAM_IO_3V3: 6.2 mm at x 42.925–43.05.
- 3V3A: 1.7–3.4 mm pairs near (29.4–40.1, 48–54).
- PYRO1_GATE: (21.6–26.0, 91.775–92.1).
- RAW_PROTECTED: (15.65/15.7, 32.35–35.75).
- Also CAM_5V, CAM_FB and NRST In2.
- VBUS_SENSE: a 3 µm same-net slot at (13.4–15.2, 71.5–71.7).

Segments < 50 µm: 287 (3V3 44, RAW_PROTECTED 16, VBUS 10, USB_LIMITED 9, 3V3A 9, CAM_5V 9, PYRO1_COLD 5, PYRO1_OUT 4).

Jogs ≤ 1 mm on critical-class nets: 55, including SWCLK ×7, VBUS_SENSE ×5 and the QSPI_IO0 staircase (12.9,42.5)→(13.5,41.9)→(14.0,41.9)→(15.6,40.3).
finding.fix:
Run a cleanup pass:
1. Merge each overlapping pair into one track of the intended width.
2. Snap endpoints to delete sub-50 µm segments.
3. Merge collinear runs and remove the jogs.
4. Rerun the gate, updating check_actuators' hashes for pyro and actuator copper deliberately.

verdicts.reasoning:
I reproduced this with my own pcbnew dump of the board (SHA-256 03fe7572…, the same file that was reviewed) and of R6 at 3b215ba shifted +18 mm in y. Tracks were tagged R6 when layer, width, net and both endpoints match within 2 µm. That gives 2,326 R6 tracks and 451 R7 tracks.

1) Overlapping parallel pairs on the same net. 119 offset pairs are R6-only. 79 of them overlap by at least 0.1 mm along their length, which is close to the claimed 76. 72 of those 79 have overlapping copper and 7 are less than 0.1 mm apart. They cluster at about 35 sites. Every quoted example is there:
- USB_LIMITED B.Cu is stacked three deep for 10.5 mm: 0.3 mm at x 28.725, plus 0.3 and 0.4 mm at x 28.7. It is doubled again for 6.05 mm at x 29.1/29.125.
- CAM_IO_3V3: 6.2 mm at x 42.925/43.05.
- 3V3A: pairs of 1.7–3.39 mm in the quoted area.
- RAW_PROTECTED: 0.6/0.4/0.25 mm tracks at x 15.65/15.7, y 32.35–35.75.
- PYRO1_GATE F.Cu: a 0.3 mm track at y 91.9 with three 0.2 mm fragments beside it at y 91.775, 91.93 and 92.1.
- CAM_5V, CAM_FB and NRST In2 also have pairs.
- VBUS_SENSE B.Cu folds back on itself. Its branches at y 71.517 and 71.67 have a 3 µm gap between them, which is a sliver.

2) Segments under 50 µm: exactly 287 on R6 copper, with the same per-net counts as claimed (3V3 44, RAW_PROTECTED 16, VBUS 10, USB_LIMITED 9, 3V3A 9, CAM_5V 9, PYRO1_COLD 5, PYRO1_OUT 4). There is one caveat: 163 of them lie inside pads and 81 inside via pads, where they change no copper. Only 43 are free-standing kinks.

3) Jogs, meaning parallel in and out segments with a middle of 1 mm or less, on R6 copper: 107 in total, 61 on power, pyro, USB, SPI/QSPI and SWD nets. The claim was 55. SWCLK has 7, including real zig-zags at (16.45–16.65, 65.75–67.65) and (23.75–24.95, 84.25–88.55). VBUS_SENSE has 5. The QSPI_IO0 staircase at (12.9,42.5)→(13.5,41.9)→(14.0,41.9)→(15.6,40.3) is R6 copper that step B kept. A few jogs with a 0.99 mm 45° middle are ordinary lateral offsets, not debris.

None of this has an electrical effect. DRC is clean, the overlaps are on the same net and merge in the Gerbers, and fab CAM usually fills a 3 µm sliver. However, the owner made clean routing an acceptance criterion for the whole board. It explicitly bans duplicate or overlapping copper, tiny jogs and zig-zags, unmerged runs and autorouter-looking debris. This is a pattern across the board on USB power, pyro gate and supply nets, so it fails that gate, and Major is right. Two numbers need correcting: the true count of overlapping pairs is higher than stated, and most of the 287 short segments are hidden inside pads or vias.
verdicts.recommended_fix:
Run a scripted R6 cleanup pass in r7_post.py, or as its own step, and finish the odd cases by hand:
1. Delete every same-net track whose copper lies entirely inside another track's copper. Where two tracks sit 25–50 µm apart side by side, keep one at the intended width, centred on its pads. Apply this to USB_LIMITED, CAM_IO_3V3, 3V3A, RAW_PROTECTED, CAM_5V, CAM_FB, NRST and PYRO1_GATE.
2. Remove sub-50 µm segments by snapping the neighbouring segment's end to the pad or via centre. The 43 free-standing ones need a real joint redraw.
3. Merge collinear runs.
4. Redraw these by hand as single clean paths: the VBUS_SENSE hairpin and its 3 µm sliver, the SWCLK zig-zags, and the QSPI_IO0 jog, which belongs in the step B reroute anyway. Leave legitimate lateral offsets alone.
5. Check that each net's pad-to-pad connectivity is unchanged. Rerun the gate (DRC 0, unconnected 0). Update the check_actuators hashes deliberately, with a diff that shows only removals and merges on pyro and actuator copper.

verdicts.reasoning:
The finding is factually correct, but two of its three counts overstate the visible problem.

Method: I made my own read-only dump with pcbnew of the board snapshot (SHA 03fe7572…, the step B hash) and of R6 at 3b215ba shifted +18 mm in y. A track counts as R6 when its layer, width and endpoints match R6 within 2 µm. That gives 2,327 R6 tracks and 450 R7 tracks, the same split the review got.

1) Overlapping copper: real, and it breaks the owner's explicit "no overlapping/duplicate copper" rule.
- 116 same-net R6 pairs overlap or sit less than 0.1 mm apart (33 on one centreline, 83 offset). In 80 of them neither track sits wholly inside the other, so the copper outline changes.
- Every cited item reproduces, all untouched R6 copper:
  - USB_LIMITED is actually tripled: 0.4 mm at x 28.7 plus 0.3 mm at x 28.7 and 28.725, for 10.5 mm. Near x 29.1 there are 0.2/0.4 mm tracks, a 0.3 mm one at x 29.125 and another at x 28.9.
  - CAM_IO_3V3 x 42.925/43.05 for 6.2 mm.
  - 3V3 x 27.8/27.9 for 5 mm.
  - A cluster of 0.3 mm 3V3A tracks offset 0.02–0.05 mm near (29.4–33.5, 48–50).
  - RAW_PROTECTED 0.6/0.4/0.25 mm stacked at x 15.65/15.7.
  - PYRO1_GATE has 0.2 mm pieces lying along its 0.3 mm run at y 92.1, 91.93 and 91.775.
  - NRST on In2 is doubled 0.135 mm apart for 2.85 mm.
  - VBUS_SENSE has a 0.003 mm same-net gap at y 71.517/71.67, a sliver for the fab's CAM.
- The review also counts 5 redundant copper loops, all from these duplicates.

2) Segments under 50 µm: 287, matching the review net by net (3V3 44, RAW_PROTECTED 16, VBUS 10, USB_LIMITED 9, 3V3A 9, CAM_5V 9, PYRO1_COLD 5). However, 244 of them lie wholly inside a same-net pad or via, none is off-angle, and they are 5–49 µm long. They don't change the copper and can't be seen. This is file housekeeping, not a visible routing defect, and it should not drive the severity.

3) Jogs: about 106 have an R6 middle segment, close to the review's 103.
- The QSPI_IO0 staircase (12.9,42.5)→(13.5,41.9)→(14.0,41.9)→(15.6,40.3) is R6 copper, untouched (all three segments tagged R6).
- More real staircases on §3 critical nets: QSPI_NCS (24.55, 42.95→42.65), QSPI_CLK, SPI1_MOSI ×2, SPI1_SCK and SPI1_MISO.
- But the count is padded. SWCLK ×7 is not a §3 critical net (§3 lists power, pyro, crystal, USB, SPI/QSPI). Many entries are ordinary 0.5–1 mm lane-shift doglegs, and some are 10–30 µm steps nobody can see.
- The review rates the same kind of jog in new copper Minor (RQ-10, RQ-11), so this part of RQ-08 is Minor too.

Severity: there is no electrical, DRC or fab consequence; the gate passes and every overlap is same-net. Even so, the owner made clean routing an acceptance criterion for the whole board. Visible duplicate copper on power, USB and pyro nets, with redundant loops and a 3 µm sliver, at about 80 sites, fails that criterion outright. The review rates the same class of defect in R7 copper Major (RQ-05). So Major stands, but on the overlap/duplicate evidence only. The micro-segment count is housekeeping, and the jogs and staircases are Minor.
verdicts.recommended_fix:
Add a deterministic cleanup stage to the build, in r7_post.py before the refill, rather than editing the board by hand.

1. For each overlapping same-net pair:
   - Delete the copy that is wholly contained in the other.
   - Replace offset doubles with one track on the main centreline at the net's intended width. Examples: USB_LIMITED as one 0.4 mm run at x 28.7 and one at x 29.1; CAM_IO_3V3 and 3V3A as single tracks; the PYRO1_GATE pieces removed.
   - Close the VBUS_SENSE 3 µm sliver by merging the y 71.517 and 71.67 runs.
   - Afterwards, confirm there are no overlap-only joints (the r5_post close_joints check), no redundant loops and zero unconnected.
2. Snap endpoints and merge collinear runs, which deletes the sub-50 µm segments as a by-product. Treat this as housekeeping; don't track it as a separate defect.
3. Straighten the genuine staircases on SPI/QSPI as a Minor follow-up: QSPI_IO0 (12.9,42.5)–(15.6,40.3), QSPI_NCS, QSPI_CLK, SPI1_MOSI/SCK/MISO. Leave the 0.5–1 mm lane-shift doglegs that obstacles force.
4. Rerun tools/check.sh and confirm the build is reproducible. Update check_actuators' pyro and actuator hashes deliberately, only after reviewing a diff of the changed PYRO1_* and RAW_ACT copper.

verdicts.reasoning:
I reproduced the finding on the live R7 board and on R6 3b215ba translated +18 mm, without touching any repo file. The core claim is right. Some sub-claims and fix steps are overstated or wrong.

**Duplicate copper (confirmed, and it fails the owner's criterion)**
- 2,324 of R7's 2,777 track segments match R6 exactly.
- 191 same-net, same-layer parallel pairs touch and overlap; 184 of them are entirely R6 copper; 108 overlap by more than 0.1 mm.
- These are whole duplicate routes, not just stray pairs:
  - USB_LIMITED: three stacked copies from U11.7 to (28.7, 57). Copies are 0.3 mm at x 28.725, 0.3 mm at x 28.7, and 0.4 mm at x 28.7 with ends shifted 0.05 mm. A third 0.3 mm variant runs via x 28.9/29.9/31.525.
  - CAM_IO_3V3: two complete parallel routes from U13.5, about 16 mm long, 25–125 µm apart.
  - PYRO1_GATE: a 0.3 mm trunk at y 91.9 enters R126.2 0.5 mm off-centre and Q124.4 0.125 mm off-centre. It is doubled by a second 0.2 mm chain with jogs, at y 92.1 / 91.93 / 91.775.
  - RAW_PROTECTED: tracks of 0.6, 0.4 and 0.25 mm stacked along x 15.65–15.7.
  - VBUS_SENSE: two routes from the via to R9.2. They leave a real 3 µm same-net slot (y 71.592–71.595).
- The owner's criterion names exactly this ("no overlapping/duplicate copper", "nothing that looks like autorouter debris"), on power, USB-power and pyro nets. So Major is justified for acceptance even though nothing is wrong electrically: DRC is 0, the overlaps are same-net, and the Gerber union is fine.

**The cleaner board fits, and the fix is mostly proportionate**
- Removing redundant copies only shrinks copper. It cannot create a clearance or pyro-spacing violation. The only risk is connectivity, and DRC plus check_r7's overlap-only-joint check catch that.
- Test on a scratch copy: I deleted the 105 segments that lie entirely inside another same-net segment, so the copper union did not change. DRC showed 0 unconnected and 5 new track_dangling ends (3V3, PYRO1_GATE, RAW_ACT_SENSE, VBUS, VLOGIC). Each needs only an endpoint re-extended.
- 84 offset R6 pairs remain after that. They need a merge into one track of the intended width with centred pad entries, not just a delete.

**Where the finding is overstated**
1. **Short segments.** There are 287 R6 segments under 50 µm (my count matches exactly). Every one is at most 1/3 of its track width, so it sits under the round end cap and shows nothing in copper. This is database hygiene (Minor). Snapping them must keep 0/45/90 angles; moving endpoints blindly would create off-angle segments.
2. **Jogs.** These are mixed.
   - Some are removable. The SWCLK zig-zag (22.85,89.45)…(25.15,84.05) has 9 segments. A 4-segment route, 45° to x 23.85, vertical, 45° to x 25.15, then vertical, keeps the same 0.173 mm minimum clearance to C127. There is no pyro bus, igniter, drain or RAW_ACT copper within 1 mm.
   - The cited QSPI_IO0 "staircase" is forced. It is a normal chamfered 2.7 mm dogleg (vertical, 45°, flat, 45°, vertical). Both straighter options hit R89.1 (3V3), at 0 and 0.026 mm. Leave it.
3. **Step 4 is wrong.** check_actuators.py hashes only m3.kicad_dru (DRU_SHA) and the pyro rule text (PYRO_RULE_SHA), and pins parts by LCSC code. It has no copper hash, so a copper cleanup needs no hash update.

**Missed by the finding**
- An R6 3V3 B.Cu segment (41.35,58.55)→(42.95,57.15) is at 41.2°, a hard break of the 0/45/90 rule.
- New R7 overlaps on PULLPIN and BAT_ILIM need the same treatment.
verdicts.recommended_fix:
Run a scripted cleanup over all copper, R6 and R7, then rerun the gate (tools/check.sh: DRC, unconnected, check_r7 overlap-only joints and C93/C100 bypass route lengths).

1. Delete every segment that lies entirely inside a same-net segment at least as wide. That is 105 segments, with no change to the copper union. Re-extend the 5 endpoints DRC then flags as dangling.
2. Collapse each remaining offset duplicate route into one track at the intended width, with centred, straight pad entries:
   - USB_LIMITED: keep the 0.4 mm route.
   - RAW_PROTECTED: one 0.6 mm trunk, then branch.
   - CAM_IO_3V3: one trunk to C93.1.
   - PYRO1_GATE: one 0.2 mm chain through R126.2, C126.1, R128.1 and Q124.4; drop the off-centre 0.3 mm trunk or the jogged chain.
   - VBUS_SENSE: one via-to-R9.2 link, which also closes the 3 µm slot.
3. Absorb segments under 50 µm and merge collinear runs, keeping only 0/45/90 angles.
4. Straighten only the jogs whose replacement passes a clearance probe, such as SWCLK by C127 (4 segments, same 0.173 mm clearance). Leave forced doglegs such as QSPI_IO0 around R89.1.
5. Fix the 41° 3V3 segment at (41.35,58.55)→(42.95,57.15).

No check_actuators hash update is needed unless m3.kicad_dru changes.
